summary: A bakery flooded and rebuilt. The member has not chosen a kind of book, so the agent must suggest one; the memories are mostly the flood and the comeback, so the right suggestion is a resilience story.

memories.title: Flour on Uncle Remy's floor
memories.body: At sixteen I swept flour off Uncle Remy's bakery floor every morning at 4 a.m. before school. He let me shape one loaf a day. Most of them were terrible. He sold them anyway, half price.

memories.title: Leaving culinary school
memories.body: I quit culinary school after one semester. The instructor called my sourdough rustic and did not mean it kindly. Uncle Remy said that just meant I needed my own oven.

memories.title: Opening day on Canal Street
memories.body: Opened Crumb & Kettle on Canal Street in Ostrander Flats with a borrowed oven and $4,000 of savings. Sold out of rye by nine. Uncle Remy bought a loaf and said nothing, which from him is applause.

memories.title: The regulars
memories.body: By now I knew the regulars by their orders: Mrs. Ilse Brandt, two seeded rolls; the night-shift nurses, whatever was left; Coach Darnell, one cinnamon knot he swore he didn't eat.

memories.title: The canal comes over
memories.body: The canal topped its banks overnight. By morning there were eleven inches of brown water in the bakery. The oven, the mixer, the flour, gone. I stood in the doorway in waders and couldn't think of one thing to do.

memories.title: Mucking out
memories.body: Thirty people showed up with shovels and shop vacs, half of them regulars. Coach Darnell brought his whole team. We carried the ruined flour sacks out in a line, like a bucket brigade in reverse.

memories.title: The insurance letter
memories.body: The insurance company said flood wasn't covered. I read the letter four times sitting in the truck. That was the only day I really thought about closing for good.

memories.title: Baking in a church basement
memories.body: Pastor Okafor let me use the church basement kitchen at night. I baked from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. and sold everything off a folding table at the Saturday farmers market.

memories.title: The prepaid loaves
memories.body: Mrs. Brandt organized a buy-a-loaf-in-advance drive. Four hundred people prepaid for bread I hadn't baked yet. I still have the clipboard with every name on it.

memories.title: Reopening
memories.body: Reopened Crumb & Kettle with a secondhand deck oven and a new floor drain. The line went around the block. I stepped into the walk-in cooler for a minute so nobody saw me cry.

memories.title: Up on cinder blocks
memories.body: Put every shelf and the new oven up on cinder blocks, eighteen inches off the floor. Customers ask why. I tell them the canal and I have an understanding now.

memories.title: Nia joins the bakery
memories.body: My daughter Nia started working mornings at the bakery. She shapes better loaves at nineteen than I did at thirty. I sell hers full price.

memories.title: Saturday bread class
memories.body: Started a Saturday bread class for kids from the Canal Street apartments that flooded with us. Ten kids, flour everywhere, one perfect braided loaf out of the whole batch.

memories.title: Dentist
memories.body: Dentist moved my cleaning to Thursday the 18th at 2:15. Bring the new insurance card.

memories.title: Truck
memories.body: Truck is due for an oil change at 82,000 miles. Also the left wiper.
